mcq.q: For \( f(x) = \sin(x) \) on \( (0, \pi) \), which expansion would be most appropriate?
Which expansion would you use for \( f(x) = x^2 \) on \( (0, L) \) if you want a series with only cosine terms?
For \( f(x) \) defined on \( (0, L) \) with \( f(0)=0 \), which expansion is guaranteed to converge to \( f(x) \) at \( x=0 \)?
If \( f(x) \) is given on \( (0, L) \) and you want a series that converges to \( f(x) \) at \( x=0 \), which expansion should you use?
When finding half-range expansions, we extend \( f(x) \) to \( (-L, L) \) to make it:

sq.q: \(\text{Given } f(x) = \begin{cases} k & 0 < x < L/2 \\ 0 & L/2 < x < L \end{cases}, \text{ find half-range cosine series.}\)
answer: \(\text{For even } n: a_n=0; \text{ for odd } n=2m-1: a_n = \frac{2k}{(2m-1)\pi}(-1)^{m+1}\)

sq.q: \(\text{Given half-range sine series } f(x) = \sum b_n \sin(\frac{n\pi x}{L}), \text{ find } b_n \text{ if } f(x) = 1.\)

lq.q: Find the Fourier series for \(f(x)=\begin{cases} \pi+x, & -\pi\leq x\leq0 \\ \pi-x, & 0\leq x\leq\pi \end{cases}\) and deduce that \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(2n-1)^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{8}\).
answer: Step Marks Since \(f(x)\) is even, \(b_n=0\) (1) \(a_0=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}(\pi-x)dx=\pi\) (2) \(a_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}(\pi-x)\cos nx\,dx=\frac{2}{n^2\pi}[1-(-1)^n]\) (4) Thus, \(f(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{4}{\pi}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(2n-1)^2}\cos(2n-1)x\) (3) Put \(x=0\): \(\pi=\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{4}{\pi}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(2n-1)^2}\) ⇒ \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(2n-1)^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{8}\) (5)
